body.name: Crescent Moon
body.tagline: Trace a Shining Slice of the Night Sky!
body.description: Connect 60 easy dots to reveal a beautiful crescent moon glowing in the night sky. This free printable helps children practise number sequencing, visual tracking, concentration, and smooth pencil control.
body.fun_fact: A crescent moon appears when sunlight illuminates only a thin curved part of the Moon that we can see from Earth.

dot_guide.heading: How to Solve the Crescent Moon Dot-to-Dot Puzzle
dot_guide.intro: A slim crescent moon is one of the most recognisable shapes in the night sky. This friendly 60-dot puzzle builds its outer curve, pointed tips, and inner arc in five manageable stages. Find dot 1 and let your moon begin to glow!
dot_guide.outro: Beautiful work—your crescent moon is shining! Add stars, sleepy clouds, or a rocket crossing the sky, then discover the ringed planet puzzle.

sections.title: The Upper Moon Tip
sections.learn: Connect dots 1 through 12 to shape the crescent's narrow upper point.
sections.fact: The Moon does not make its own light; it shines by reflecting sunlight.

sections.title: The Outer Curve
sections.learn: Continue from dot 13 to dot 24 along the broad outside curve of the Moon.
sections.fact: Gravity made the Moon nearly round, just as it makes planets round.

sections.title: The Lower Moon Tip
sections.learn: Follow dots 25 through 36 to form the lower point and turn toward the inside curve.
sections.fact: The Moon's surface is covered with craters made by rocks striking it over billions of years.

sections.title: The Inner Crescent
sections.learn: Trace dots 37 through 48 up the inner arc, keeping your pencil line smooth.
sections.fact: The Moon takes about 29.5 days to move through a complete cycle of phases.

sections.title: The Glow and Finish
sections.learn: Finish with dots 49 through 60 to close the crescent and add its final details.
sections.fact: People around the world see the same Moon, although its crescent can appear tilted differently depending on location.

body.name: Ringed Planet
body.tagline: Draw a World Wrapped in Shining Rings!
body.description: Connect 43 easy dots to reveal a beautiful ringed planet floating in space. This free printable helps younger children practise number order, visual tracking, concentration, and steady pencil control.
body.fun_fact: Saturn's rings are made of countless pieces of ice and rock, ranging from tiny grains to chunks as large as houses.

dot_guide.heading: Can You Solve This Ringed Planet Dot-to-Dot Puzzle?
dot_guide.intro: Far beyond Earth, a giant planet turns while broad rings sweep around it. This friendly 43-dot puzzle creates the planet and its rings in four short stages, making it a fun first space challenge. Find dot 1 and begin your journey!
dot_guide.outro: Wonderful work—your ringed planet is orbiting among the stars! Add moons, a rocket, and colourful clouds, then continue exploring with the space rover puzzle.

sections.title: The Top of the Planet
sections.learn: Connect dots 1 through 11 to draw the curved upper edge of the distant planet.
sections.fact: Planets look round because gravity pulls their material toward the centre from every direction.

sections.title: The First Ring
sections.learn: Continue from dot 12 to dot 22 to trace the first wide arc of the ring system.
sections.fact: Saturn has thousands of narrow ringlets that look like several broad rings when viewed from far away.

sections.title: The Planet's Lower Curve
sections.learn: Follow dots 23 through 33 around the lower half of the planet, keeping the curve smooth.
sections.fact: Saturn is a gas giant made mostly of hydrogen and helium, the two lightest elements.

sections.title: The Rings and Finish
sections.learn: Finish with dots 34 through 43 to complete the sweeping rings on the other side.
sections.fact: Saturn's rings are very wide but surprisingly thin compared with the size of the planet.

body.name: Space Rover
body.description: Connect 59 dots to reveal a friendly space rover ready to explore another world. This free printable puzzle helps children practise number order, concentration, and pencil control.
body.fun_fact: Space rovers are robotic vehicles that explore the surfaces of worlds such as the Moon and Mars.

dot_guide.heading: Connect the Dots to Reveal the Space Rover
dot_guide.intro: Ready for a trip beyond Earth? Follow the numbers from 1 to 59 and watch a friendly space rover appear. Move slowly, check each number, and keep your pencil lines neat as you travel around the vehicle.
dot_guide.outro: Mission complete—your space rover is ready to explore! Add stars, craters, planets, or a friendly alien to create your own space scene.

sections.title: The Rover Body
sections.learn: Begin at dot 1 and connect through dot 12 to trace the rover's friendly front and sturdy body.
sections.fact: Planetary rovers carry computers, cameras, and scientific tools inside a tough body.

sections.title: The First Wheels
sections.learn: Continue from dot 13 to dot 25 to shape the lower body and the first rugged wheel.
sections.fact: Rover wheels are designed to grip loose sand and roll over rocks without getting stuck.

sections.title: The Wheel System
sections.learn: Connect dots 26 through 38 to complete more of the rover's wheels and suspension.
sections.fact: NASA's Mars rovers use a rocker-bogie suspension that helps all six wheels stay on uneven ground.

sections.title: The Seat and Equipment
sections.learn: Trace dots 39 to 49 to add the seat and equipment above the rover body.
sections.fact: Some lunar rovers carry astronauts, while robotic rovers explore without anyone sitting inside.

sections.title: The Dish Antenna
sections.learn: Finish by joining dots 50 through 59 to complete the communication dish.
sections.fact: A rover uses antennas to send discoveries to Earth and receive new instructions.
